question: What list of models does Jev choose from at dispatch — the static `dispatch.models` in `.sober/config.jsonc`, or one built against the live catalogues (`claudeModels`, `codexModels`, `openRouterModels` in packages/core/src/models.ts)?

options.label: Config list as written (today)
options.reason: ADR 0061: a model is named by a person, with a range that is a budget decision. Jev reads `about` and picks. No network before a dispatch, deterministic, and the config is the whole truth.
options.costLater: A free OpenRouter model that was retired keeps its entry until somebody notices a failed start; a new free one is invisible until `sober models` is run by hand and `sober models add` typed. The list drifts from what exists.

options.label: Config list, pruned against the catalogue
options.reason: Every entry stays a human choice, but at dispatch an opencode entry whose model is no longer in OpenRouter's catalogue (or a codex entry missing from `~/.codex/models_cache.json`) is dropped before Jev sees it, and the dispatch log says so.
options.costLater: One HTTPS call to openrouter.ai per dispatch (cacheable in `.sober/local`); an OpenRouter outage must not stop a dispatch, so the prune is best-effort and a stale entry can still slip through. New models still need a hand-typed entry.

options.label: Whole catalogue, filtered by per-host rules and a denylist
options.reason: Jev sees everything the three catalogues list today (`claudeModels`, `codexModels`, `openRouterModels`), narrowed by a new `dispatch.sources` block instead of a hand-typed model list: per source a complexity range and an optional `only`/`deny` of id patterns — e.g. `openrouter-free: { complexity: [1,3] }`, `claude: { complexity: [6,10], deny: ["fable*"] }`, `codex: { complexity: [6,10], deny: ["*astra*"] }`. A retired model vanishes on its own, a new free one appears on its own, and a model you never want to pay for cannot be picked. `dispatch.models` stays for pinning a hand-named entry, with preference over discovered ones.
options.costLater: Jev's prompt carries the filtered catalogue (tens of free entries), so its choice is noisier and `about` is the provider's blurb, not yours; a brand-new free model with a broken provider is picked before anybody tried it, and the run record names a model nobody wrote down (the backup catches the failure, not the waste). A catalogue call per dispatch, cached in `.sober/local`; OpenRouter down means the opencode source is empty for that dispatch, logged. Claude's catalogue is still the hand-written constant in models.ts, so a new Claude model is a code change. ADR 0061 is amended and `sober models` gains a `--sources` view so what Jev would see is checkable by hand.

options.label: Catalogue only, ranges per host, no denylist
options.reason: Same as above without `only`/`deny`: least config, and every model a host can reach is fair game within its range.
options.costLater: Nothing keeps Jev off the most expensive model in a range — Fable at complexity 6 is a legal pick — so cost control is only the range, and the range is per host not per model. Otherwise the same costs as the constrained shape.
